scope_statement: Literature on theoretical mechanisms of platform economies limited to explicitly listed platform concepts only.
must_cover: Direct and indirect network externalities, positive and negative
Critical mass, growth paths, and chicken–egg dilemma
Multi-homing and switching costs impact on lock-in
Platform governance: rules, rankings, access controls
Monetization and pricing structures, fees and commissions
Competitive dynamics: tipping, winner-takes-most versus coexistence
should_cover: Formal models of platform growth and tipping
Empirical measures of network effects and quality
Interactions between pricing and network effects
Design levers for stabilizing multi-sided interactions
must_avoid: Additional market or organization theories beyond listed concepts
Transaction cost economics and similar frameworks
Resource-based view or firm-level organizational theories
Industrial organization theories beyond platform mechanisms
main_query: platform mechanisms two-sided markets network externalities critical mass multi-homing governance monetization competition
facet_queries: platform governance rules ranking access control
scoring_guidance: Prioritize sources explicitly addressing the listed platform concepts; prefer peer-reviewed theoretical and empirical work, recent high-quality studies, clear method and relevance to chapter scope.
